newsitem.title: CANADA: Crystallex sinks after Venezuelan ruling.
newsitem.headline: Crystallex sinks after Venezuelan ruling.

text.p: Shares in Crystallex International Corp sank more than 50 percent on Wednesday after Venezuela's Supreme Court ruled on the company's long-running dispute with Placer Dome Inc over the Las Cristinas gold property.
Crystallex's stock closed down 4.20 at 3.80 in active turnover of 3.17 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange. The share price earlier hit a low of 3.20.

Investors dumped the stock despite Crystallex's statement on Wednesday that the court on Tuesday rendered a favorable ruling on the company's rights to concessions 4 and 6 of the rich Las Cristinas property.
Crystallex has argued that its unit, Inversora Mael, was the rightful owner of the concessions.
"The ruling in no way confirms, or even mentions, the validity of the alleged mining rights claimed by Placer Dome," Ricardo Cottin, Crystallex's Venezuelan counsel said in a statement.
An independent legal source told Reuters that the court's decision was preliminary and would inevitably be appealed.
Lawyers for Vancouver-based Placer Dome have argued the court's ruling was clearly in its favor. Placer stock gained 1.05 to 21.50 on 903,000 shares on Wednesday.
"The implication (from the Venezuelan court ruling) is that, for the next little while, it should put to rest any claims," said John Ing, president of brokerage Maison Placements Canada Inc.
Venezuelan government officials have insisted throughout the dispute that Crystallex's claim was unjustified and that the joint venture in which Placer holds a 70 percent stake would proceed.
Ing said he expected Placer Dome to prevail because it had the financial resources to develop the project.
"I think ultimately Placer will be able to put it into production," he said.
